in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 18 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 18 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 18 (which is over 16), I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is 18 and in approved education (doing his A-levels), that's good for eligibility purposes - you can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education.

Now I need to ask about your own circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**You mentioned Alex lives at home with you - can you confirm that you're responsible for him? This typically means you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, accommodation, and general living expenses.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. I'm responsible for him - he lives here with me and I provide for all his needs like food, clothes, and everything else he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, another parent or guardian?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started any paid work. He's just focusing on his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful, thank you. Just one final question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that actually - I don't know if he's receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's okay. Let me explain why this matters and then provide you with my assessment.

Children normally stop being eligible for Child Benefit if they start claiming certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit. However, since Alex is living at home with you, focusing on his A-levels, and not in paid work, it's unlikely he would be claiming such benefits (as these are typically for people who are unable to work due to disability, or who are on low income and working/seeking work).

Based on all the information you've provided, I now have enough to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me provide you with my decision.

## **Good News - You Are Eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!**

Based on all the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:
- Alex is 18 years old and is in approved education (his A-level course at college)
- You can continue to receive Child Benefit for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training
- You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex, who lives at home with you
- You provide for all his needs
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He's not working 24+ hours per week
- There's no indication of disqualifying factors

**Important Note:** Please be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit but may need to pay back some or all of it through your tax return.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he finishes or leaves his A-level course, starts working 24+ hours a week, or starts claiming certain benefits), you'll need to inform HMRC as this could affect your eligibility.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
